open_points.subject: closure status of R0-91 to R0-99
open_points.text: None open. ... R0-91 to R0-99 (2026-11-23) answer Q1 to Q9 of the data-protection requirements matrix.
open_points.question: How can these questions be closed when R0-91, R0-93, R0-94, R0-97 and R0-99 expressly leave blocking, a customer-download operation, retention-page design, durable security logging and write-count enforcement to later owner decisions?
options: Declare those deferred matters open questions
Remove the prospective promises and close only the current behavior
Decide every deferred matter in State 0
open_points.default_guess: List each deferred matter as an open question and treat only the explicitly stated current behavior as closed.

witness.initial: State 0 is handed to a later designer with the Open questions section saying none are open.
events: The designer reads R0-94 saying blocking and the review-page design are decided later by a new owner decision.
The designer must decide whether those features belong in the next design.
outcomes: The designer treats the questions as closed and invents the features.
The designer treats them as unresolved and omits the features pending another owner decision.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing the later design

open_points.subject: LOPDGDD blocking applicability
open_points.text: Whether any value it holds — a customer's contact or fiscal data, an object's address — must be blocked after erasure rather than erased is a question for the legal review of the governance ... A legal answer that some Registry value must be blocked is a new owner decision here.
open_points.question: Which Registry values, if any, must enter blocking instead of being erased, what starts and ends blocking, and what must Registry return while they are blocked?
options: No Registry value is blocked; erasure remains final
Block specified customer fields
Block specified project/object fields
Block an entire customer or project record atomically
open_points.default_guess: Keep the stated current rule: Registry erases, and implement no blocking until a new owner decision specifies it.

open_points.subject: machine-readable data-subject copy
open_points.text: The machine-readable copy is the owner's, assembled from those reads. Registry gains no operation for it now.
open_points.question: What exact machine-readable format, schema, field set, identifiers, metadata, encoding and failure result must the owner produce?
options: A documented JSON schema
A collection of Registry's existing JSON responses
CSV files
A portable archive combining Registry and other-service data
open_points.default_guess: Produce a documented JSON object containing the existing read results and governance-supplied metadata.

witness.initial: A customer has one active project, one archived project and several artifacts.
events: The owner performs the reads named in R0-93.
outcomes: The owner sends a single normalized JSON document.
The owner sends an archive of unrelated raw API responses with different field shapes.
witness.observer: The requesting customer and any system importing the copy

open_points.subject: customer-with-projects review and download operation
open_points.text: A read-only owner operation that gathers a customer with every project naming it, as one page and a JSON download, is a candidate change once the first release is assembled; adopting it is a new owner decision here.
open_points.question: Is this operation part of the product promise, and if so what records, archived projects, anonymised projects, artifacts and errors does it include?
options: Adopt the page and JSON operation now
Explicitly reject it
Leave it outside the product until a separately recorded decision
open_points.default_guess: Leave it outside the implementation until a separate owner decision adopts and specifies it.

open_points.subject: data-subject request procedure
open_points.text: the procedure that answers a data subject's request (R0-93) ... [is] kept as platform-wide governance ... outside this case
open_points.question: Who receives a request, verifies the requester and their authority, records its receipt and deadline, coordinates answers from all services, records partial refusal, and proves completion or failure?
options: A named manual owner procedure with recorded evidence
A platform-wide workflow
Independent procedures in every service
open_points.default_guess: Use one documented owner-led procedure with identity verification, a request register, deadlines, service checklists and recorded outcomes.

open_points.subject: retention review page delivery
open_points.text: After the first release is assembled, it gains a read-only review page ... The design of both is decided then, by a new owner decision here.
open_points.question: Is the review page already required, or must implementation wait for another decision; and what event objectively means that the first release is assembled?
options: Specify and require the page in this decision
Make it an explicit open question with no present implementation obligation
Define a release/version milestone that activates an already specified page
open_points.default_guess: Treat the page as uncommitted until a new owner decision supplies its complete design.

witness.initial: The first release passes its tests, but no later owner decision about the page exists.
events: A later agent designs the next release.
The agent must interpret the words 'it gains' and 'design ... is decided then'.
outcomes: The agent builds a retention review page by inventing its behavior.
The agent omits the page because the required owner decision has not occurred.
witness.observer: The owner performing the retention review

open_points.subject: retention-period configuration
open_points.text: the customers whose relationship ended, and the archived projects archived, longer ago than periods the owner sets in the configuration from the schedule
open_points.question: What configuration keys, units, defaults and validation rules represent each period, and what does the page do when a period is absent, invalid or changed?
options: Separate validated periods for customer and project data
One common retention period
No default and refuse to render until all periods are configured
Use provisional R0-40 periods as defaults
open_points.default_guess: Use separate validated day-based periods with no silent default; show a configuration error when a required period is missing.

open_points.subject: retention review page contents
open_points.text: a read-only review page in the owner interface: the customers whose relationship ended, and the archived projects archived, longer ago than periods the owner sets in the configuration from the schedule
open_points.question: What fields, ordering, boundary comparison, pagination and eligibility explanations does the page show, and does it also show audit entries due for erasure?
options: Show only due customers and projects
Also show audit entries due for erasure
Show every retained record with due/not-due reasons
open_points.default_guess: Show due customers, projects and audit entries, ordered oldest first, with the anchor date, applicable period and computed due date.

open_points.subject: Client Portal copy propagation
open_points.text: Client Portal's offline projection (R0-39) is Portal's; whether Portal keeps one and how it follows a change is stated in Portal's case
open_points.question: When Registry corrects, erases or restricts data already held in Portal's offline projection, who communicates or applies that change, by what trigger, within what time, and what happens while Portal is offline?
options: Portal refreshes on every use and deletes stale data
Registry sends a change notification
The owner manually triggers Portal correction or erasure
Portal may serve the stale projection until its own expiry
open_points.default_guess: Require Portal to refresh or invalidate its projection on reconnect and define a maximum offline lifetime.

witness.initial: Portal holds an offline projection containing an address that Registry later corrects or erases.
events: The owner changes the Registry record.
The home connection remains unavailable while Portal serves its projection.
outcomes: Portal continues showing the old address.
Portal invalidates the projection and stops showing it until refreshed.

open_points.subject: erasure from Registry backups
open_points.text: Registry's backups lose an erased value within the period A18 states.
open_points.question: What is that period, when does it start, what operation removes or expires the value, and what is observable if a backup is restored before expiry?
options: Expire whole backups after a fixed retention period
Rewrite backups to remove erased values
Allow restoration but immediately replay erasures
Treat restored erased data as live again
open_points.default_guess: Expire whole encrypted backups on a stated fixed schedule and require erasure reconciliation after any restore.

open_points.subject: writer guidance for room names and aliases
open_points.text: That description is changed with the changes planned after the first release is assembled ... until then the rule binds the owner, and the agent through the governance's instructions to it.
open_points.question: What exact text and interaction teach the rule in the owner interface and manifest, who changes them, and what happens if either surface still carries the old description?
options: Inline owner-interface guidance plus normative manifest descriptions
Governance instructions only
A confirmation before each write
Automated content validation
open_points.default_guess: Put the same normative rule in inline owner-interface help and both manifest field descriptions, without claiming automated enforcement.

open_points.subject: post-first-release change bundle
open_points.text: After the first release is assembled, with the changes R0-93, R0-94 and R0-96 planned, Registry counts refused attempts in memory
open_points.question: Does counting activate independently, only when all referenced changes are adopted, or in one atomic release; and which R0-93 change is meant when its gathering operation is only a candidate?
options: Ship all changes atomically
Ship refusal counting independently
Wait until separate owner decisions adopt every candidate change
open_points.default_guess: Treat refusal counting as an independent versioned feature and state its activation release explicitly.

open_points.subject: refused-attempt counter categories
open_points.text: refused sign-ins and lockouts; calls on the service API with a token Registry does not know; calls whose token does not allow the operation or class asked; and, apart from these, Kernel's agent-authority calls refused for a session or a project outside its set
open_points.question: Are refused sign-ins and lockouts one counter or two, can one request increment multiple counters, how are nonexistent sessions separated from out-of-set projects, and which other refusals are excluded?
options: One mutually exclusive counter per listed category
Multiple applicable counters per request
One aggregate counter with reason metadata
open_points.default_guess: Use mutually exclusive counters, with separate counters for failed sign-ins and lockout events and a documented precedence order.

witness.initial: The owner is already locked out.
events: Another wrong sign-in is attempted during the lockout.
Registry later restarts and the owner signs in successfully.
outcomes: The attempt increments both 'refused sign-in' and 'lockout'.
The attempt increments only one counter under a precedence rule.
witness.observer: The owner viewing the first page after sign-in

open_points.subject: in-memory counter scope
open_points.text: Registry counts refused attempts in memory from its start ... a restart clears them
open_points.question: Is the count per process, per worker, per Registry instance or shared across workers, and what exactly constitutes the start or restart shown to the owner?
options: One process and one counter set
Aggregate counters shared by all workers in the instance
Show separate counters and start times per worker
open_points.default_guess: Define one logical Registry instance with a single aggregated in-memory counter set and one startup instant.

open_points.subject: security-event visibility during lockout
open_points.text: shows them to the owner on the first page after sign-in
open_points.question: How can the owner learn why sign-in is refused while locked out, and when is the first successful opportunity to see the counters if attempted access continues?
options: Show a non-sensitive lockout reason on the refused sign-in page
Expose counters only after lockout expiry
Require a restart to clear lockout
Provide a separate owner recovery procedure
open_points.default_guess: Show a generic lockout status and expiry without attempt details before sign-in, then show the counters after successful sign-in.

open_points.subject: DPIA screening completion
open_points.text: the screening's likely conclusion is that a DPIA is not required ... the screening ... is made now, in parallel
open_points.question: Who performs and approves the screening, what recorded output constitutes completion, by when must it finish, and what happens if it concludes that a DPIA is required?
options: Named governance owner records and approves the screening before a stated date
Independent reviewer performs it
Import proceeds regardless and the result only changes later governance
A high-risk result triggers a defined DPIA and mitigation gate
open_points.default_guess: Assign a named governance owner, require a dated recorded decision, and define a high-risk result as triggering a DPIA and mitigation plan.

open_points.subject: precondition concerning the legacy objects folder
open_points.text: It holds once the owner's earlier machine no longer gives the agent the objects folder (the cleanup step of the home server's move).
open_points.question: Who performs and verifies this cleanup, what evidence proves the agent has lost access, and may the screening conclusion or continued processing be relied on before that verification?
options: Make verified cleanup a prerequisite
Allow processing while recording a temporary exception
Treat cleanup as unrelated to Registry and make no platform claim until completed
open_points.default_guess: Require a recorded access test proving removal before relying on the stated no-DPIA conclusion.

open_points.subject: standing approval binding
open_points.text: Each such write of the agent waits for the owner's approval of its exact request, unless the owner gave that flow version a standing approval for the node
open_points.question: Which request fields and contextual facts make an approval exact, and is it invalidated by a flow-version change, node change, project change, session change, record revision or manifest-contract change?
options: Bind approval to the complete canonical request and all context
Bind it only to flow version and node
Bind it to operation and project
Let Kernel define the binding without a Registry requirement
open_points.default_guess: Bind approval to flow version, node identity, operation, canonical request, session, project, expected revision and manifest contract version.

open_points.subject: standing approvals inside collection maps
open_points.text: The governance's rule is that no standing approval is given to a node that writes to Registry inside a map over a collection.
open_points.question: Who detects that a node is inside such a map, who prevents the standing approval, and what observable failure occurs if the owner attempts to grant one?
options: Kernel technically refuses the approval
The owner interface hides or disables the approval
It is only a procedural rule and an invalid approval can still run
Registry rejects writes made under such an approval
open_points.default_guess: Require Kernel to refuse creation or use of the standing approval and return a specific policy failure.

open_points.subject: future Registry write-count enforcement
open_points.text: A count enforced by Registry is reconsidered, by a new owner decision here, if standing approvals for such writes become needed.
open_points.question: What condition means standing approvals have become needed, and what limits, time window, scope and failure behavior would Registry enforce?
options: Never add a Registry count; rely on approvals
Set per-run limits
Set per-session or per-project rate limits
Set per-operation configurable quotas
open_points.default_guess: Keep no Registry count now and record this as an explicit open question triggered by a concrete request for mapped standing approvals.
